ARES-Twin is a Physical AI Marswalk Co-Navigator, Monte Carlo Digital Twin, and SPOC/AI4Mars Helmet Visor HUD built for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge (available as both a zero-install browser app and a Python FastAPI full-stack system).

To address the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge, ARES-Twin fuses five official NASA data streams into an interactive surface navigation platform for Gale Crater (Mount Sharp) and Jezero Crater: JPL Mars Trek MOLA and Viking WMTS layers, USGS SIM 3292 geologic unit context, live Curiosity and Perseverance MMGIS rover traverses (1,389 and 708 waypoints), real Mastcam/Navcam raw surface imagery, and NASA Worldview/GIBS aerosol calibration. It runs uncertainty-aware EVA path planning and simulated helmet-HUD terrain segmentation directly over real Martian topography.

Because Mars-to-Earth communication delays prevent real-time mission control guidance during an EVA, astronauts need autonomous, hazard-aware situational awareness. ARES-Twin bridges orbital maps and ground-level rover vision to help explorers avoid steep slopes, dust-obscured terrain, and wheel-trapping hazards—making future Marswalks safer and mission-ready.
details:
## What It Does & How It Works

ARES-Twin is a Physical AI Marswalk Co-Navigator, Monte Carlo Digital Twin, and SPOC/AI4Mars-inspired Helmet Visor HUD built for Extravehicular Activity (EVA) planning and surface navigation in Gale Crater (Mount Sharp) and Jezero Crater. It is delivered in two editions: a zero-install pure browser prototype (Option A) and a full-stack Python FastAPI + Physical AI backend (Option B).

The system fuses five official NASA and USGS data streams into a unified operational interface:

1. Orbital Basemaps (JPL Mars Trek WMTS): Live MOLA color-shaded relief (463m) and Viking global optical mosaic (232m) tile layers.

2. Planetary Geology (USGS SIM 3292): Tanaka et al. (2014) geologic unit context for Gale Crater and Jezero Crater.

3. Rover Ground Truth (NASA MMGIS & Science Resources): Real Curiosity traverse data (1,389 waypoints up to Sol 5073) and Perseverance traverse data (708 waypoints up to Sol 2022), anchored to Curiosity's proposed path up Mount Sharp.

4. Surface Vision (Mars Raw Images API): Real Mastcam, Mastcam-Z, and Navcam POV frames fed into the Helmet Visor HUD (`vision_ai.py`) for terrain/hazard segmentation overlays.

5. Atmospheric Calibration (NASA Worldview / GIBS): MODIS Terra reflectance and OMPS Aerosol Index layers used as Earth-analog dust and visibility calibration references.

On top of these datasets, the backend's `physics_engine.py` and `planner.py` compute terrain-aware EVA routes and Monte Carlo uncertainty envelopes, helping explorers compare baseline paths against hazard-avoiding trajectories.

## Benefits & Intended Impact

Because Mars-to-Earth light-time communication delays prevent real-time guidance from Mission Control, surface crews need autonomous onboard decision support. ARES-Twin bridges the gap between high-level orbital maps and first-person ground imagery—allowing astronauts and mission planners to preview steep slopes, dust-degraded visibility, and loose-regolith hazards before committing to an EVA traverse. Our goal is to make future human and robotic Mars surface operations safer, faster to plan, and more resilient.

## Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

- Backend: Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, NumPy, Pillow, HTTPX, Pydantic (`main.py`, `nasa_client.py`, `physics_engine.py`, `planner.py`, `vision_ai.py`)

- Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas, OGC WMTS tile streaming

- Data Tooling & Packaging: Custom NASA dataset bundler (`scripts/build_nasa_bundle.py`), Git, and GitHub

## Creativity & Factors Considered

- Dual-Deployment Design: Offering both an instant zero-install web app and a full Python AI/physics backend ensures anyone—from astronauts in bandwidth-constrained habitats to judges testing locally—can run it immediately.

- Grounded in Real Mission Heritage: Instead of synthetic terrain alone, navigation is anchored to actual Curiosity and Perseverance rover traverses and real Mars surface camera frames.

- Offline Resilience & Dust Realism: We accounted for intermittent deep-space connectivity by bundling deterministic local NASA data caches alongside live API fetching, and modeled atmospheric dust/visibility degradation using NASA GIBS aerosol benchmarks.
